title: GTA 6 opening weekend sales: $2 billion forecast
description: GTA 6 opening weekend sales could top $2 billion, says analyst Joost van Dreunen, per Eurogamer. Here's the maths behind the forecast and the risks.

body.text: GTA 6 opening weekend sales could top $2 billion, according to a forecast from analyst Joost van Dreunen, reported by Eurogamer. If he's right, Rockstar's next game would comfortably beat the milestone GTA 5 set, and it could give a nervous games industry a lift at a time when it badly needs one.
GTA 6 opening weekend sales: how the maths works
First, the benchmark. GTA 5 passed $1 billion in its first three days on sale. Take-Two believed at the time that no entertainment property, music and films included, had reached that figure faster.
Van Dreunen, a senior data analyst, laid out his prediction in his SuperJoost PlayList newsletter. He expects Take-Two to announce opening-weekend sales above $2 billion by Monday, 23rd November.

His reasoning starts with pre-orders. Eurogamer says a conservative estimate of 10 million is circulating, backed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick. The game is also reportedly tracking well above even the company's high expectations. At roughly $100 a copy, that is about $1 billion before anyone has played it. Van Dreunen says that is two days faster than GTA 5 got there. The second billion, he argues, arrives over the launch weekend.

A big part of the story is how many buyers are choosing the pricier Ultimate Edition, listed at £90. Eurogamer reports that Take-Two raised its forecast to $3.5 billion for the next financial quarter, citing "recurrent consumer spending". Zelnick explained on an investor call that this is explicitly tied to the Ultimate Edition.
So the higher price tag is already feeding into the company's numbers, not just the analyst's spreadsheet.
First-year sales and the bigger picture

Van Dreunen expects roughly another 28 million copies over the first year, which would put GTA 6 at 38 million. That is only modestly ahead of GTA 5's 35 million. In his view, the real difference could be how much revenue each player generates in the years afterwards.

He also thinks the game could lift the whole industry. He sees it as a counterweight to AI-generated filler and mobile games built purely to extract money, and as proof that spending heavily on a game people actually want can still pay off. Eurogamer adds that this could be a welcome jolt after rampant layoffs and shrinking talent pools, even for readers who are sceptical of Rockstar's motives.

It isn't all good news for Rockstar. Eurogamer notes the studio is facing legal action over accusations of union busting, after more than 30 employees were fired. The conclusion of that case is due this week, just as the game goes on sale.

Keep an eye on Take-Two's announcement after launch weekend. Van Dreunen's call is a prediction, not a confirmed figure, so the real numbers will show whether $2 billion was realistic. Also watch the outcome of the legal case, and whether Ultimate Edition demand keeps driving the spending Take-Two is counting on.

faqs.q: How much could GTA 6 make in its opening weekend?
faqs.a: Analyst Joost van Dreunen predicts Take-Two will announce opening-weekend sales above $2 billion by Monday, 23rd November, according to Eurogamer.

faqs.q: How many GTA 6 pre-orders are there?
faqs.a: Eurogamer reports a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders, backed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick. It also says the game is tracking well above the company's expectations.

faqs.q: How many copies could GTA 6 sell in its first year?
faqs.a: Van Dreunen forecasts first-year sales of 38 million copies, slightly ahead of GTA 5's 35 million, per Eurogamer.
